meta.title: Tantric Prayer
meta.subtitle: Thirty-Six Prayers for the Inner Weather
meta.blurb: the nine rasas · four prayers each · kashmir shaivism
meta.epi_iast: api labdhabhavadbhāvaḥ svātmollāsamayaṃ jagat / paśyan bhaktirasābhogair bhaveyam aviyojitaḥ
meta.epi_en: seeing the world as the delight of the self — may i never be parted from it, through the enjoyment of devotion's rasa.

sections.title: Śṛṅgāra
sections.gloss: śṛṅgāra — "amorous sentiment, love; the beauty that adorns" (Monier-Williams)
sections.doctrine: sthāyin: rati — the beloved becomes the light of consciousness; separation is its fuel (Abhinavabhāratī)

sections.title: Hāsya
sections.gloss: hāsya — "laughable, comic; mockery — that which slays" (from hās, to slay)
sections.doctrine: sthāyin: hāsa — the world-as-joke; laughter is the register of the play seen from inside

sections.title: Karuṇā
sections.gloss: karuṇā — "compassion, mercy; the pitiable, what moves to pity"
sections.doctrine: sthāyin: śoka — “all rasas are essentially pleasurable, even the painful” — grief is bliss in a minor key (Abhinavabhāratī)

sections.title: Raudra
sections.gloss: raudra — "furious, stormy — the mood of Rudra" (rudra: to roar)
sections.doctrine: sthāyin: krodha — anger exists because it is one with the wonder that is the experience of consciousness (Tantrāloka 15254)

sections.title: Vīra
sections.doctrine: sthāyin: utsāha — enthusiasm is the energy of recognition, not of the task

sections.title: Bhayānaka
sections.doctrine: sthāyin: bhaya — fear is real even when its object is a rope; use the realness, skip the object (Abhinavabhāratī, rope-snake)

sections.title: Bībhatsa
sections.gloss: bībhatsa — "loathsome, revolting; that which excites disgust"
sections.doctrine: sthāyin: jugupsā — disgust points at the un-looked-at; the cure is darśana, seeing

sections.title: Adbhuta
sections.doctrine: sthāyin: vismaya — wonder (camatkāra) is the primary characteristic of consciousness itself (Tantrāloka ad 1/53)

sections.title: Śānta
sections.gloss: śānta — "pacified, allayed, put to rest" — the ninth, added by Abhinavagupta
sections.doctrine: sthāyin: śānti — the ninth rasa, Abhinavagupta's own addition: the ocean in which the other eight swim
